title: Lalithaa Jewellery Mart's Rs 1,700-Crore IPO Opens With Strong Investor Interest
excerpt: The Chennai-based jewellery chain's public offering, priced at a steep discount to listed peers, signals growing appetite for organized retail jewellery stocks in India.
body:
• Lalithaa Jewellery Mart's Rs 1,700-crore IPO opened for subscription on August 17 at a price band of Rs 190-201 per share
  • The Chennai-based chain operates 61 stores across South India, with 45 in tier-II and tier-III cities generating over 60% of revenue
  • At a post-issue P/E of roughly 10x, the offering is priced at a significant discount to listed peer Kalyan Jewellers, which trades above 46x earnings
  • Proceeds will fund 10 new stores and inventory expansion as the company targets deeper penetration in underpenetrated southern markets

Lalithaa Jewellery Mart, one of South India's largest organized jewellery retailers, opened its initial public offering on August 17 in what analysts are calling one of the more attractively priced mainboard IPOs of the year. The issue, which closes on August 19, has drawn strong early interest from retail investors, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

The company has set the price band at Rs 190 to Rs 201 per equity share, valuing the total offering at approximately Rs 1,700 crore. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to Rs 1,200 crore and an offer for sale of up to Rs 500 crore by promoter M. Kiran Kumar Jain, who serves as chairman and managing director.

A South Indian Jewellery Powerhouse

Founded in 1985, Lalithaa Jewellery operates 61 stores across 51 cities in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, and the Union Territory of Puducherry. The company sells BIS-hallmarked gold, silver, and diamond jewellery, with competitive pricing driven by its in-house manufacturing capabilities.

What distinguishes the company from larger national chains is its deliberate focus on smaller cities. In fiscal 2026, 45 of its 61 stores were located in tier-II and tier-III cities, contributing 60.25% of total revenue, according to a CRISIL report cited in the offer documents. The company's total operational area spans 650,881 square feet, with both large-format stores exceeding 15,000 sq. ft. and medium-format locations above 5,000 sq. ft.

"45 of our 61 stores are in tier-II and tier-III cities, contributing to 60.25 per cent of revenues."

— M. Kiran Kumar Jain, Chairman and Managing Director

Valuation Gap Draws Attention

The IPO's most compelling feature may be its pricing. At the upper band of Rs 201, the post-issue price-to-earnings ratio works out to roughly 10x based on fiscal 2026 earnings, where the company reported revenue of approximately Rs 25,040 crore and profit after tax of around Rs 1,010 crore. That represents a return on net worth of 39.9%.

By comparison, listed peer Kalyan Jewellers India trades at a trailing P/E above 46x, while other organized jewellery retailers command significantly richer multiples. The valuation gap, combined with strong profitability metrics, has led several market analysts to view the offering favorably.

Grey market premiums have indicated potential listing gains of around 15%, though analysts caution that GMP is an unofficial, unregulated indicator that can shift sharply before listing day.

Growth Plans and Market Context

The company plans to use Rs 1,200 crore in fresh issue proceeds primarily to fund the opening of 10 new stores, covering both capital expenditure for store fit-outs — including furniture, fixtures, equipment, and IT infrastructure — and the substantial inventory costs that jewellery retail demands. A portion will go toward general corporate purposes.

The offering comes amid sustained demand for organized jewellery retail in India, where the sector remains highly fragmented. South India, in particular, has seen rapid formalization as consumers in smaller cities increasingly prefer branded, hallmarked products over unorganized local jewellers.

Investors can bid for a minimum lot of 74 equity shares at a minimum investment of Rs 14,874. Anchor investor allocation took place on August 14, and Anand Rathi Advisors and Equirus Capital are serving as book-running lead managers. Shares are expected to list on both the BSE and NSE on August 24.
nri_angle: Lalithaa Jewellery's IPO offers NRI investors exposure to India's fast-growing organized jewellery retail sector at a valuation well below listed peers.
